Cardiac fibroma.description: A rare benign primary cardiac tumor composed of fibroblasts and abundant collagen, usually arising within ventricular myocardium in infants or children. It is typically a firm, well-circumscribed intramyocardial mass.

Cardiac myofibroma.description: A benign myofibroblastic tumor that may occur congenitally and can rarely involve the heart. Histology commonly shows spindle-cell proliferation, collagen, and branching thin-walled vascular channels.

Cardiac rhabdomyoma.description: The most common fetal and pediatric cardiac tumor, usually a benign hamartomatous lesion of cardiac muscle. It is strongly associated with tuberous sclerosis complex and often regresses after birth.

Cardiac hemangioma.description: A rare benign vascular tumor of the heart that can arise in the myocardium, endocardium, or pericardium. It consists of proliferating vascular channels and may be detected incidentally or prenatally.

Acute pyelonephritis with focal bacteria.normalized_text: Acute pyelonephritis with focal bacterial nephritis
Acute pyelonephritis with focal bacteria.description: Acute bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma; focal bacterial nephritis is a localized, non-liquefactive inflammatory renal mass that can appear wedge-shaped or mass-like on imaging.

Renal infarction.description: Renal infarction is ischemic necrosis of renal tissue caused by occlusion of a renal arterial branch or the main renal artery, often producing peripheral wedge-shaped lesions and absent perfusion.

Renal abscess.description: A renal abscess is a localized collection of pus within the kidney, usually developing as a complication of ascending pyelonephritis or hematogenous bacterial spread.

Renal vein thrombosis.description: Renal vein thrombosis is clot formation in the renal venous drainage, which may cause renal enlargement, parenchymal edema, reduced venous flow, hematuria, and impaired renal function.

Renal cell carcinoma.description: Renal cell carcinoma is a malignant epithelial tumor of the kidney that may present as a solid renal mass with variable vascularity, hemorrhage, necrosis, or invasion of renal vessels.

Fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma.description: A distinct subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma that often occurs in younger patients without cirrhosis and commonly appears as a large hepatic mass with a central fibrous scar, sometimes containing calcification.

Focal nodular hyperplasia.description: A benign hyperplastic liver lesion, often incidentally found, characterized by a central stellate fibrous scar and typically occurring in otherwise normal liver tissue.

Hepatic adenoma.description: A benign hepatocellular tumor that may become large and heterogeneous because of hemorrhage, necrosis, or fat content; it is often associated with estrogen exposure, anabolic steroids, obesity, or metabolic disease.

Conventional hepatocellular carcinoma.description: A primary malignant tumor of hepatocytes, most commonly arising in a cirrhotic liver or in patients with chronic hepatitis B or C infection; large tumors can become heterogeneous from necrosis or hemorrhage.

Dominant optic atrophy (OPA1-related her.normalized_text: Dominant optic atrophy (OPA1-related hereditary optic neuropathy)
Dominant optic atrophy (OPA1-related her.description: A hereditary mitochondrial optic neuropathy causing slowly progressive, usually bilateral and symmetric optic nerve dysfunction with temporal optic disc pallor and retinal nerve fiber layer loss.

Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON).description: A maternally inherited mitochondrial optic neuropathy that typically causes painless central visual loss, often sequentially involving both eyes, with peripapillary vascular tortuosity early and later optic atrophy.

Bilateral optic neuritis related to mult.normalized_text: Bilateral optic neuritis related to multiple sclerosis or other inflammatory demyelinating disease
Bilateral optic neuritis related to mult.description: Inflammation and demyelination of the optic nerves can cause visual loss, impaired color vision, pain with eye movement, and eventual optic atrophy with retinal nerve fiber layer thinning.

Normal-tension glaucoma or advanced prim.normalized_text: Normal-tension glaucoma or advanced primary open-angle glaucoma
Normal-tension glaucoma or advanced prim.description: A chronic optic neuropathy characterized by progressive retinal ganglion-cell and retinal nerve fiber loss, optic disc cupping, and corresponding visual field defects; it can occur even with normal intraocular pressure.

Nutritional, toxic, or medication-relate.normalized_text: Nutritional, toxic, or medication-related optic neuropathy
Nutritional, toxic, or medication-relate.description: Bilateral toxic or nutritional optic neuropathy causes symmetric retinal ganglion-cell injury and optic atrophy, commonly with painless progressive central visual loss and color vision impairment.

Wilson disease (hepatolenticular degener.description: An autosomal-recessive disorder caused by ATP7B dysfunction, resulting in impaired copper excretion, copper accumulation in the liver, brain, and cornea, and hepatic and neurologic disease.

Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumu.description: A group of inherited neurodegenerative disorders characterized by excessive iron deposition in the basal ganglia, often causing dystonia, parkinsonism, cognitive decline, and characteristic MRI changes.

Manganese deposition due to chronic live.normalized_text: Manganese deposition due to chronic liver disease or portosystemic shunting
Manganese deposition due to chronic live.description: Manganese accumulation in the basal ganglia can occur in advanced chronic liver disease or portosystemic shunting and typically produces bilateral T1 hyperintensity in the globus pallidus, sometimes with parkinsonian neurologic manifestations.

Dermatitis herpetiformis.description: A chronic, intensely itchy autoimmune blistering skin disease associated with gluten sensitivity/celiac disease, typically causing grouped papules, vesicles, and excoriations on extensor surfaces.

Plaque psoriasis.description: A chronic inflammatory skin disorder producing well-demarcated erythematous plaques with scale, commonly affecting the elbows and other extensor surfaces.

Atopic dermatitis (eczema).description: A pruritic inflammatory dermatitis that can cause erythematous papules, patches, excoriations, and chronic thickened skin; it may involve the elbows, especially in adults.

Allergic or irritant contact dermatitis.description: An inflammatory skin reaction caused by direct contact with an allergen or irritant, producing localized redness, itching, papules, vesicles, or plaques.

Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis.normalized_text: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH, Forestier disease)
Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis.description: A noninflammatory enthesopathic disorder characterized by bulky, flowing ossification of ligaments and entheses, commonly along the anterior longitudinal ligament of the spine.

Cervical spondylosis with large anterior.normalized_text: Cervical spondylosis with large anterior osteophytes
Cervical spondylosis with large anterior.description: Age-related degenerative disease of the cervical spine involving disc degeneration, vertebral endplate changes, and osteophyte formation.

Ankylosing spondylitis.description: A chronic inflammatory spondyloarthritis that can cause spinal ankylosis through formation of thin marginal syndesmophytes and fusion of spinal joints.

Insulinoma.description: A pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that secretes insulin autonomously, causing endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.

Sulfonylurea or meglitinide-induced hypo.description: Hypoglycemia caused by insulin secretagogue medications, which stimulate pancreatic beta cells to release endogenous insulin.

Insulin autoimmune syndrome (Hirata dise.description: A rare autoimmune condition in which insulin autoantibodies bind and later release insulin, producing spontaneous episodes of hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia without exogenous insulin exposure.

Non-insulinoma pancreatogenous hypoglyce.description: Diffuse pancreatic beta-cell hyperfunction causing excessive endogenous insulin secretion, often associated with postprandial hypoglycemia and sometimes occurring after bariatric surgery.

Slipping rib syndrome.description: A condition in which hypermobile false ribs, usually the 8th to 10th ribs, move excessively at their cartilaginous attachments and may slip beneath an adjacent rib, irritating intercostal nerves.

Rib fracture with displacement or healin.normalized_text: Rib fracture with displacement or healing callus
Rib fracture with displacement or healin.description: A break in a rib that may produce cortical irregularity, step-off deformity, displacement, or callus formation during healing.

Congenital rib or costal-cartilage anoma.description: A developmental variation in rib shape, spacing, fusion, or costochondral anatomy that can alter the appearance and relationship of adjacent ribs.

Pneumatosis cystoides intestinalis.description: A condition characterized by multiple gas-filled cysts within the bowel wall, often affecting the colon. It may be benign/idiopathic or secondary to bowel, pulmonary, infectious, ischemic, or medication-related conditions.

Colonic lymphangiomatosis (multiple colo.description: A benign malformation of lymphatic vessels that can produce multiple submucosal cystic lesions in the gastrointestinal tract, usually containing clear lymphatic fluid rather than gas.

Colonic pneumatosis due to bowel ischemi.normalized_text: Colonic pneumatosis due to bowel ischemia
Colonic pneumatosis due to bowel ischemi.description: Intramural bowel gas caused by intestinal ischemia or infarction, often associated with severe abdominal pain and potentially life-threatening bowel injury. Imaging may show linear or cystic gas in the bowel wall.

Colonic polyposis syndrome.description: A group of disorders characterized by numerous colorectal polyps, including adenomatous, hamartomatous, or serrated polyps; these lesions arise from mucosa rather than being gas-filled intramural cysts.

Leucemia eosinofílica crónica, no especi.normalized_text: Leucemia eosinofílica crónica, no especificada de otra manera (CEL-NOS)
Leucemia eosinofílica crónica, no especi.description: Una neoplasia mieloide clonal caracterizada por hipereosinofilia persistente, maduración anormal de eosinófilos, citopenias y/o displasia, tras la exclusión de causas reactivas y específicas asociadas al gen de fusión de eosinofilia.

síndrome mielodisplásico con eosinofilia.normalized_text: síndrome mielodisplásico con eosinofilia y der(1; 7)(q10; p10) anomalía
síndrome mielodisplásico con eosinofilia.description: Una neoplasia mieloide con producción ineficaz de células sanguíneas y displasia. Cromossoma derivado 1; 7 anomalías recurrentes en síndromes mielodisplásicos y pueden estar asociadas con anemia, displasia multilineal y eosinofilia.

Neoplásia mielodisplásica/mieloprolifera.description: Un grupo de solapamiento de trastornos mieloides clonales que muestran tanto hematopoyesis displásica como características proliferativas como eosinofilia o aumento de precursores mieloides. Se necesitan pruebas moleculares para distinguir esto de CEL-NOS y neoplasias eosinofílicas asociadas a fusión.

Neoplasia mieloide/linfoide con eosinofi.normalized_text: Neoplasia mieloide/linfoide con eosinofilia y reordenamiento génico de tirosina-quinasa (por ejemplo, reordenamiento de PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 o PCM1-JAK2)
Neoplasia mieloide/linfoide con eosinofi.description: Un grupo de neoplasias hematológicas clonales impulsadas por reordenamientos que involucran genes tirosina-quinasa. Comúnmente causan eosinofilia marcada y pueden producir anemia, hallazgos displásicos de médula y síntomas constitucionales o de afectación orgánica.

diagnoses.name: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma
diagnoses.normalized_text: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma

Rosai-Dorfman disease (sinus histiocytos.normalized_text: Rosai-Dorfman disease (sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy)
Rosai-Dorfman disease (sinus histiocytos.description: A rare non-Langerhans-cell histiocytic disorder characterized by accumulation of S100-positive histiocytes, often showing emperipolesis on histology. It can cause painless lymphadenopathy and extranodal disease involving the gastrointestinal tract, kidneys, skin, and other organs.

Langerhans cell histiocytosis.description: A clonal histiocytic neoplasm involving Langerhans cells, which may affect bone, skin, lungs, lymph nodes, liver, spleen, and occasionally the gastrointestinal tract. Lesions typically express CD1a and langerin (CD207).

Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.description: A malignant proliferation of lymphoid cells that can present with generalized lymphadenopathy, abdominal masses, bowel infiltration, renal lesions, and bowel obstruction, particularly in pediatric or young patients.

IgG4-related disease.description: A systemic fibroinflammatory disorder characterized by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, often with increased IgG4-positive plasma cells. It can involve lymph nodes, kidneys, retroperitoneum, pancreas, and gastrointestinal structures.

Malaria por Plasmodium falciparum.description: Una malaria potencialmente grave causada por P. falciparum, caracterizada por alta parasitemia, hemólisis, trombocitopenia, disfunción hepática y posible lesión renal. La prueba diagnóstica rápida y la citología periférica que muestra parásitos en forma de anillo, incluidos múltiples anillos dentro de los eritrocitos, apoyan firmemente este diagnóstico.

Malaria falciparum grave con hemólisis y.normalized_text: Malaria falciparum grave con hemólisis y lesión renal aguda
Malaria falciparum grave con hemólisis y.description: Una forma grave de malaria por P. falciparum en la que la destrucción de eritrocitos infectados y la captura microvascular causan hemólisis, ictericia, trombocitopenia, elevación de enzimas hepáticas y disfunción renal.

Babesiosis.description: Una infección protozoaria intraeritrocítica transmitida por garrapatas que puede causar anemia hemolítica, trombocitopenia, ictericia, elevación de enzimas hepáticas y disfunción renal. Puede parecerse a la malaria en una citología periférica, pero normalmente muestra tétradas cruzadas de Malta en lugar del patrón clásico de P. falciparum.

Fiebre del dengue con trombocitopenia se.normalized_text: Fiebre del dengue con trombocitopenia severa
Fiebre del dengue con trombocitopenia se.description: Una enfermedad viral transmitida por mosquitos que puede producir trombocitopenia, leucopenia o linfopenia, hemoconcentración, transaminasas elevadas y fugas de plasma. El dengue severo puede causar hemorragias, shock y disfunción orgánica.

Esophageal perforation with mediastiniti.description: A full-thickness tear or rupture of the esophageal wall allows saliva, gastric contents, and bacteria to enter the mediastinum, causing severe inflammation and infection.

Acute suppurative mediastinitis.description: A serious bacterial infection of the mediastinum, often caused by esophageal perforation, surgery, or spread from an oropharyngeal infection.

Iatrogenic esophageal perforation.description: An esophageal tear caused by a medical procedure such as endoscopy, dilation, stent placement, surgery, or instrumentation; it may lead to contrast extravasation and mediastinal infection.

Esophageal leak following esophageal sur.normalized_text: Esophageal leak following esophageal surgery or endoscopic intervention
Esophageal leak following esophageal sur.description: Leakage from a surgical anastomosis, esophageal repair site, or endoscopic intervention can result in mediastinal contamination, abscess formation, and purulent drainage.

Hodgkin lymphoma.description: A malignant lymphoma characterized by lymph-node enlargement and possible involvement of the spleen, mediastinum, and pleura.

Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.description: A diverse group of lymphoid malignancies that may cause widespread lymphadenopathy, splenic enlargement, thoracic involvement, and pleural effusions.

Chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymph.description: A mature B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder that can produce generalized lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and occasionally pleural involvement.

Disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculo.normalized_text: Disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculous lymphadenitis and pleuritis
Disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculo.description: Mycobacterial infection that can cause cervical lymphadenopathy, pleural effusion, pulmonary abnormalities, and splenic involvement in disseminated disease.

Hepatic encephalopathy.description: A reversible neuropsychiatric syndrome caused by liver dysfunction and accumulation of neurotoxins such as ammonia. EEG commonly shows generalized, frontally predominant triphasic waves.

Metabolic or toxic encephalopathy.description: Diffuse brain dysfunction due to systemic metabolic abnormalities or toxins, including electrolyte disturbances, medication effects, sepsis, hypoxia, or organ failure. Triphasic waves may occur.

Uremic encephalopathy.description: Cerebral dysfunction caused by severe renal failure and accumulation of uremic toxins. EEG typically demonstrates generalized slowing and can show triphasic waves.

Nonconvulsive status epilepticus.description: Ongoing seizure activity without prominent convulsive movements, often presenting with impaired awareness or unexplained encephalopathy. Generalized periodic discharges can overlap electrographically with triphasic waves and require clinical correlation.

Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.description: A rapidly progressive prion neurodegenerative disorder that can produce periodic sharp-wave complexes on EEG, usually in the setting of rapidly progressive dementia and myoclonus.

Bartholin gland cyst.description: A benign mucus-filled cyst caused by obstruction of the Bartholin gland duct, typically located posterolaterally at the vaginal introitus.

Bartholin gland abscess.description: An infected Bartholin gland cyst that produces a painful vulvar mass and may show inflammatory changes or rim enhancement on imaging.

Epidermal inclusion cyst of the vulva/pe.normalized_text: Epidermal inclusion cyst of the vulva/perineum
Epidermal inclusion cyst of the vulva/pe.description: A benign keratin-containing cyst that may occur in the vulvar or perineal soft tissues, often after trauma, surgery, or local skin obstruction.

Gartner duct cyst.description: A benign embryologic remnant cyst usually arising from the anterolateral upper vaginal wall.

Susac syndrome.description: A rare autoimmune endotheliopathy affecting small vessels of the brain, retina, and inner ear. Its classic triad is branch retinal artery occlusion, encephalopathy/characteristic corpus callosum lesions, and sensorineural hearing loss.

Multiple sclerosis.description: A chronic immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that can produce white-matter and corpus callosum lesions, visual symptoms, and occasionally auditory symptoms.

Branch retinal artery occlusion due to e.normalized_text: Branch retinal artery occlusion due to embolic or vascular disease
Branch retinal artery occlusion due to e.description: Occlusion of a retinal arterial branch, commonly caused by an embolus, vascular risk factors, vasculitis, or hypercoagulability, leading to focal retinal ischemia and a corresponding visual-field defect.

Cogan syndrome.description: A rare systemic inflammatory vasculitis characterized primarily by inflammatory ocular disease and audiovestibular dysfunction, including sensorineural hearing loss; retinal vascular inflammation can occur but is less typical.

Mitochondrial myopathy due to an mtDNA m.normalized_text: Mitochondrial myopathy due to an mtDNA m.3243A>G variant (MELAS-spectrum disorder)
Mitochondrial myopathy due to an mtDNA m.description: A maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder that can cause myopathy, exercise intolerance, elevated creatine kinase, neurologic manifestations including seizures, and characteristic ragged-red/respiratory-chain-deficient muscle fibers. Adult-onset axial weakness can present as camptocormia (bent-spine syndrome).

Myoclonic epilepsy with ragged-red fiber.description: A mitochondrial DNA disorder, most often related to the m.8344A>G MT-TK variant, characterized by myoclonic epilepsy, mitochondrial myopathy, elevated CK, and ragged-red fibers on muscle biopsy.

Mitochondrial DNA maintenance disorder /.normalized_text: Mitochondrial DNA maintenance disorder / adult-onset mitochondrial myopathy
Mitochondrial DNA maintenance disorder /.description: Nuclear-gene defects affecting mitochondrial DNA replication or maintenance, such as POLG, TWNK, or OPA1-related disorders, can produce adult-onset mitochondrial myopathy with axial weakness, elevated CK, seizures, and abnormal mitochondrial staining on muscle biopsy.

Myofibrillar myopathy presenting with ca.description: A group of inherited muscle diseases caused by disruption of myofibrillar structural proteins, including desmin, filamin C, BAG3, or myotilin. They may cause axial and paraspinal weakness, bent-spine syndrome, and mild-to-moderate CK elevation.

diagnoses.name: B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable, with features intermediate between diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and Burkitt lymphoma
diagnoses.normalized_text: B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable, with features intermediate between diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and Burkitt lymphoma
diagnoses.icd11_title: B-cell lymphoma unclassifiable with features intermediate between Burkitt lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

Burkitt lymphoma/leukemia.description: An aggressive mature B-cell neoplasm characterized by very rapid proliferation, often with MYC rearrangement involving chromosome 8 and an immunoglobulin gene locus. When extensive marrow and blood involvement is present, it is termed Burkitt leukemia.

B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymp.description: A precursor B-cell malignancy causing marrow replacement by lymphoblasts, commonly presenting with circulating blasts and cytopenias. It is usually defined by immaturity markers such as TdT and lacks the classic mature B-cell/MYC-driven Burkitt pattern.

Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, high-grad.normalized_text: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC rearrangement
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, high-grad.description: An aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma composed of large atypical B cells. Some cases harbor MYC rearrangement and can involve marrow and blood, although classic Burkitt morphology and isolated MYC-driven disease favor Burkitt lymphoma/leukemia.

Acute myeloid leukemia.description: A clonal myeloid malignancy with accumulation of immature myeloid blasts in bone marrow and blood. Diagnosis requires myeloid lineage markers and/or defining genetic abnormalities.

Hepatic metastases.description: Secondary malignant deposits in the liver from a cancer arising elsewhere, commonly producing multiple focal liver lesions.

Primary hepatic lymphoma.description: Lymphoma involving the liver, which may appear as solitary or multiple hypodense hepatic lesions and can be associated with splenic involvement.

Hepatic sarcoidosis.description: Granulomatous inflammatory disease that can involve the liver and spleen, producing multiple small hypodense nodules and hepatosplenomegaly.

Multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma.description: Primary liver cancer that can present with multiple hepatic nodules, especially in a liver affected by chronic hepatitis or cirrhosis.

Hepatic microabscesses.description: Multiple small infectious collections in the liver, often caused by bacterial, fungal, or opportunistic infection and sometimes associated with splenic lesions.

diagnoses.name: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
diagnoses.icd11_title: Acute ST segment elevation myocardial infarction

Acute proximal left anterior descending.normalized_text: Acute proximal left anterior descending coronary artery occlusion (de Winter T-wave pattern, anterior STEMI equivalent)
Acute proximal left anterior descending.description: A high-risk ECG pattern associated with acute proximal LAD coronary occlusion. It typically shows upsloping ST-segment depression with prominent, symmetric hyperacute T waves in the anterior precordial leads rather than classic ST elevation.

Acute anterior myocardial infarction wit.normalized_text: Acute anterior myocardial infarction with hyperacute T waves
Acute anterior myocardial infarction wit.description: Early acute anterior myocardial infarction from LAD ischemia can initially produce broad, prominent hyperacute T waves before typical ST-segment elevation and Q waves develop.

Hyperkalemia.description: Elevated serum potassium can cause tall, narrow-based peaked T waves, followed by PR prolongation, P-wave flattening, QRS widening, and potentially malignant arrhythmias as severity increases.

Bronchopulmonary sequestration (likely l.description: A congenital nonfunctioning segment of lung tissue that lacks normal bronchial communication and receives systemic arterial blood supply, commonly from the descending aorta. Extralobar sequestration often occurs near the left lower thorax or diaphragm.

Intralobar pulmonary sequestration.description: A form of pulmonary sequestration located within a normal lung lobe, usually in a posterior lower lobe, with anomalous systemic arterial supply from the aorta. It may cause recurrent infection or respiratory symptoms.

Hybrid congenital pulmonary airway malfo.normalized_text: Hybrid congenital pulmonary airway malformation with sequestration
Hybrid congenital pulmonary airway malfo.description: A congenital lung malformation containing features of both congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) and pulmonary sequestration, often presenting as a lower-lobe mass with cystic elements and anomalous systemic arterial supply.

Congenital diaphragmatic hernia or diaph.normalized_text: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia or diaphragmatic eventration
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia or diaph.description: A congenital abnormality of the diaphragm that permits abdominal contents to elevate into the chest or causes persistent elevation of a hemidiaphragm, potentially compressing the adjacent lung and causing respiratory distress.

Malignant hypertension (hypertensive eme.normalized_text: Malignant hypertension (hypertensive emergency with hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis)
Malignant hypertension (hypertensive eme.description: Severe acute hypertension causing concentric smooth-muscle and intimal proliferation in arterioles, producing an "onion-skin" appearance and marked luminal narrowing; fibrinoid necrosis may also occur.

Scleroderma renal crisis.description: A life-threatening complication of systemic sclerosis characterized by abrupt severe hypertension and renal vascular injury, including intimal proliferation and onion-skin narrowing of renal arterioles.

Thrombotic microangiopathy.description: A syndrome of endothelial injury and small-vessel thrombosis, such as that seen in hemolytic uremic syndrome, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, severe hypertension, or drug-related injury. Chronic lesions can show intimal swelling and concentric vascular narrowing.

Chiari I malformation.description: A structural abnormality in which the cerebellar tonsils extend downward through the foramen magnum, potentially crowding the cervicomedullary junction and impairing cerebrospinal fluid flow.

Basilar invagination with ventral brains.normalized_text: Basilar invagination with ventral brainstem compression
Basilar invagination with ventral brains.description: An upward displacement of the upper cervical spine toward the skull base that can narrow the foramen magnum and compress the lower brainstem or upper cervical spinal cord.

Craniocervical instability.description: Excessive motion or abnormal alignment between the skull, atlas, and axis that may cause intermittent compression or stretching of the brainstem and upper cervical spinal cord; dynamic flexion-extension MRI can help evaluate it.

Leukonostok turlari yuqtiruvchi endokard.description: Leuconostoc tomonidan yuzaga keladigan infeksion endokardit, vankomistinga o'zidan chidamli gram-musbat kokk/kokobasillus hisoblanadi. U vayronkor mahalliy yoki protez klapan infektsiyasiga olib kelishi mumkin va enterokoklar bilan adashtirilishi mumkin.

Vankomissinga chidamli enterokokk infeks.description: Enterokokk turlari tomonidan orttirilgan vankomisin rezistentligiga ega bo'lgan endokardit. Enterokoklar odatda subakut yoki og'ir klapalar infeksiyasini keltirib chiqaradi va sefalosporinlarga tabiiy chidamlilikka ega.

Lactobacillus turlari yuqtiruvchi endoka.description: Lactobacillus endokarditi — bu kamdan-kam uchraydigan invaziv infeksiya bo'lib, gram-musbat tayoqchalar tomonidan yuzaga keladi, ular ko'pincha vankomitsinga ichki chidamlilikka ega va katta vayronkor klapan o'simliklarini hosil qilishi mumkin.

Weissella turi yuqumli endokardit.description: Weissella kamdan-kam uchraydigan vankomissinga chidamli gram-musbat kokkobasillus bo'lib, bakteriemiya va kamdan-kam hollarda infeksion endokarditga sabab bo'lishi mumkin. U laboratoriya sinovlarida viridans streptococci, Leuconostoc yoki enterokoklarga o'xshash ko'rinishi mumkin.

Acute pulmonary embolism.description: Obstruction of a pulmonary artery by thrombus, typically originating from a deep vein thrombosis. The CT image shows a filling defect within a left pulmonary arterial branch, which is characteristic of pulmonary embolism.

Chronic pulmonary thromboembolism.description: Persistent organized thrombus in the pulmonary arteries after prior embolic events; it may lead to chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.

Pulmonary artery tumor embolus or pulmon.normalized_text: Pulmonary artery tumor embolus or pulmonary artery sarcoma
Pulmonary artery tumor embolus or pulmon.description: Rare malignant tissue within or obstructing a pulmonary artery that can mimic thromboembolism on contrast-enhanced CT.

Herpes simplex virus encephalitis.description: An acute viral encephalitis, most commonly caused by HSV-1, with a characteristic predilection for the medial temporal lobes, inferior frontal lobes, insulae, and limbic structures.

Autoimmune limbic encephalitis.description: An immune-mediated inflammatory disorder involving the limbic system, often associated with antibodies such as LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B receptor, AMPA receptor, or paraneoplastic antibodies.

Seizure-related peri-ictal MRI abnormali.description: Transient cortical and mesial temporal MRI signal abnormalities can occur after prolonged focal seizures or status epilepticus, particularly involving the hippocampi and temporal lobes.

Neurosyphilis or other infectious limbic.normalized_text: Neurosyphilis or other infectious limbic encephalitis
Neurosyphilis or other infectious limbic.description: Central nervous system infection from syphilis or other pathogens can cause meningoencephalitis and, less commonly, medial temporal or limbic inflammatory MRI abnormalities.

Neumonía grave por Legionella (enfermeda.normalized_text: Neumonía grave por Legionella (enfermedad del legionario)
Neumonía grave por Legionella (enfermeda.description: Una neumonía bacteriana atípica grave causada por especies de Legionella que puede provocar insuficiencia respiratoria, hiponatremia, elevación de enzimas hepáticas, rabdomiólisis e inflamación sistémica.

Neumonía bacteriana grave con sepsis.description: Una infección bacteriana pulmonar grave puede causar insuficiencia respiratoria aguda, leucocitosis neutrofílica, disfunción orgánica relacionada con sepsis, anomalías metabólicas y lesiones miocárdicas.

Neumonía grave por COVID-19 con respuest.normalized_text: Neumonía grave por COVID-19 con respuesta hiperinflamatoria
Neumonía grave por COVID-19 con respuest.description: La infección grave por SARS-CoV-2 puede causar insuficiencia respiratoria aguda, inflamación sistémica, hiperferritinemia, lesión miocárdica, anomalías enzimáticas hepáticas y lesiones musculares.

Linfostiocitosis hemofagocítica secundar.normalized_text: Linfostiocitosis hemofagocítica secundaria (HLH) / síndrome de activación de macrófagos
Linfostiocitosis hemofagocítica secundar.description: Un síndrome hiperinflamatorio potencialmente mortal caracterizado por una activación inmunitaria excesiva, a menudo desencadenada por infecciones o malignidades, con hiperferritinemia, lesión hepática, citopenias u otras anomalías hematológicas, y disfunción multiorgánica.

Crisis suprarrenal aguda.description: La insuficiencia suprarrenal aguda es una emergencia endocrina que puede causar hiponatremia, hiperpotasemia, hipoglucemia o, ocasionalmente, hiperglucemia de estrés, hipotensión y shock; puede desencadenarse por una infección grave.

Tumorframkallað osteomalaci orsakað av f.normalized_text: Tumorframkallað osteomalaci orsakað av fosfaturiskum mesenkymalum tumor
Tumorframkallað osteomalaci orsakað av f.description: Eitt sjáldsamt paraneoplastiskt syndrom, sum er orsakað av einum vanliga lítlum mesenkymalum tumori, sum framleiðir ov nógv FGF23. FGF23 elvir til nýrafosfat minking, skerda aktivering av vitamin D, hypofosfatemi og osteomalasiu. Skurðviðgerð av tumorinum rættar vanliga biokemiskar óreglur.

Primær hyperparathyroidismi.description: Ein sjúka við sjálvvirkandi yvirskoti av parathyroid hormoni, oftast frá parathyroid adenoma. Hon orsakar vanliga hypercalcemia, hægri ella óhóskandi normal PTH, økt beinskifti og stundum lágt fosfat orsakað av nyrnafosfatminking.

X-bundin hypofosfatemi ella onnur arvali.normalized_text: X-bundin hypofosfatemi ella onnur arvalig, FGF23-miðlað hypofosfatemisk raket/osteomalasi
X-bundin hypofosfatemi ella onnur arvali.description: Arvaligar sjúkur, sum eru eyðkendar av ov nógvari FGF23-virksemi, sum elvir til langvarandi nýrafosfatminking, lágt fosfat, skerda beinmineralisering og hægri alkalisk fosfatasa. Tær byrja vanliga í barnalagnum og hvørva ikki eftir at ein fokalur tumor er tikin burtur.

Infective endocarditis with systemic emb.description: Infection of the endocardial surface, usually involving a cardiac valve, with vegetations that can embolize to the brain, spleen, kidneys, and other organs.

Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis.description: Sterile platelet-fibrin vegetations on cardiac valves, often associated with malignancy, autoimmune disease, or hypercoagulable states, which frequently cause arterial embolic infarctions.

Libman-Sacks endocarditis associated wit.normalized_text: Libman-Sacks endocarditis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus or antiphospholipid syndrome
Libman-Sacks endocarditis associated wit.description: A form of sterile verrucous endocarditis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus and antiphospholipid antibodies; valvular vegetations can cause thromboembolic stroke and other systemic infarcts.

Cardioembolic ischemic stroke due to an.normalized_text: Cardioembolic ischemic stroke due to an intracardiac thrombus or valvular thrombus
Cardioembolic ischemic stroke due to an.description: A thrombus arising from the heart or a cardiac valve can embolize into systemic arteries, producing acute ischemic stroke and infarctions in abdominal organs.

Cranioectodermal dysplasia (síndrome de.description: Ciliopatía autosómica recesiva, frecuentemente asociada con variantes en IFT122, WDR35, IFT43 u otros genes del transporte intraflagelar. Produce craneosinostosis/dolicocefalia, displasia esquelética de costillas y extremidades, alteraciones ectodérmicas y enfermedad renal progresiva.

Distrofia torácica asfixiante de Jeune.description: Ciliopatía esquelética autosómica recesiva caracterizada por tórax estrecho con costillas cortas, acortamiento de extremidades, braquidactilia y posible enfermedad renal, hepática y retiniana progresiva.

Síndrome de Mainzer-Saldino.description: Ciliopatía generalmente autosómica recesiva que combina displasia esquelética con falanges cortas, enfermedad renal tubulointersticial o nefroptisis y alteraciones oculares, especialmente distrofia retiniana.

Síndrome de Ellis-van Creveld.description: Displasia esquelética ciliopática caracterizada por extremidades cortas, tórax estrecho, costillas cortas, polidactilia frecuente y anomalías ectodérmicas dentales y ungueales; pueden existir cardiopatías congénitas.

Dermatomyositis.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy characterized by distinctive skin findings, often including Gottron papules over the knuckles; muscle weakness and systemic involvement may occur.

Clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis.description: A subtype of dermatomyositis with characteristic cutaneous findings but little or no clinically apparent muscle weakness; it may still be associated with internal organ disease or malignancy.

Cutaneous lupus erythematosus.description: An autoimmune skin disease that can cause photosensitive erythematous or scaly plaques and may occur with systemic lupus erythematosus.

Psoriasis.description: A chronic immune-mediated skin disease producing well-demarcated erythematous plaques with scale; it may involve the hands and joints.

Allergic or irritant contact dermatitis.normalized_text: Allergic or irritant contact dermatitis of the hands
Allergic or irritant contact dermatitis.description: Inflammation of the skin caused by exposure to irritants or allergens, commonly producing redness, scaling, fissuring, and itching on the hands.

Legg-Calve-Perthes disease.description: Childhood osteonecrosis of the femoral head epiphysis, causing sclerosis, fragmentation, flattening, and possible enlargement or deformity of the femoral head.

Bilateral femoral head osteonecrosis (av.description: Loss of blood supply to the femoral heads leading to collapse, sclerosis, fragmentation, flattening, and secondary degenerative deformity. It may occur with corticosteroid exposure, sickle cell disease, trauma, or other systemic conditions.

Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.description: An inherited skeletal dysplasia characterized by delayed, irregular, flattened, or fragmented epiphyses, often affecting both hips symmetrically and predisposing to early osteoarthritis.

Meyer dysplasia of the femoral head.normalized_text: Meyer dysplasia of the femoral head
Meyer dysplasia of the femoral head.description: A benign developmental variant in young children with delayed and irregular ossification of the femoral head epiphyses, often bilateral and sometimes mistaken for Perthes disease.

Chilaiditi sign / Chilaiditi syndrome.description: Interposition of colon, usually the hepatic flexure or transverse colon, between the liver and right hemidiaphragm. When symptomatic, it is termed Chilaiditi syndrome and can mimic free intraperitoneal air.

Pneumoperitoneum due to hollow-viscus pe.description: Free air within the peritoneal cavity, commonly caused by perforation of the stomach, duodenum, bowel, or another hollow abdominal organ; this is usually a surgical emergency when associated with peritonitis.

Subphrenic abscess.description: A localized infected fluid collection beneath the diaphragm, often occurring after abdominal surgery, perforation, trauma, or intra-abdominal infection. It may contain gas if caused by gas-forming organisms or communication with bowel.

Right hemidiaphragm eventration or diaph.normalized_text: Right hemidiaphragm eventration or diaphragmatic elevation
Right hemidiaphragm eventration or diaph.description: Abnormal elevation of an intact hemidiaphragm due to congenital thinning, phrenic nerve dysfunction, or reduced lung volume. It can alter the position of abdominal organs and facilitate colonic interposition.

Periventricular nodular heterotopia.description: A neuronal-migration malformation in which nodules of gray matter remain along the walls of the lateral ventricles instead of reaching the cerebral cortex. It commonly presents with seizures and may be associated with other developmental brain abnormalities.

Subcortical band heterotopia (double cor.description: A developmental neuronal-migration disorder characterized by an abnormal band of gray matter within the cerebral white matter, often bilateral and symmetric. Affected individuals may have epilepsy and variable developmental impairment.

FLNA-associated periventricular nodular.description: An often X-linked form of periventricular nodular heterotopia caused by FLNA variants. It typically produces bilateral periventricular gray-matter nodules and may be associated with epilepsy, cardiovascular abnormalities, and connective-tissue features.

diagnoses.name: Primary yolk sac tumor of intestine
diagnoses.normalized_text: Primary yolk sac tumor of intestine
diagnoses.icd11_title: Yolk sac tumour, unspecified site, female

Primary hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the j.normalized_text: Primary hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the jejunum
Primary hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the j.description: A rare, aggressive intestinal adenocarcinoma showing hepatocellular-like differentiation, often with AFP and glypican-3 expression and high FDG uptake.

Primary jejunal adenocarcinoma with ente.normalized_text: Primary jejunal adenocarcinoma with enteroblastic differentiation
Primary jejunal adenocarcinoma with ente.description: A rare subtype of intestinal adenocarcinoma with fetal gastrointestinal/enteroblastic differentiation, which may express AFP, glypican-3, and SALL4 and may have reduced expression of conventional intestinal markers.

Conventional primary small-intestinal ad.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising from the small-intestinal mucosa, usually forming invasive glands and commonly expressing broad-spectrum cytokeratins and intestinal markers.

Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma invo.normalized_text: Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma involving the jejunum
Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma invo.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma can rarely metastasize to the gastrointestinal tract and may express AFP and glypican-3, mimicking hepatoid adenocarcinoma.

Extragonadal yolk sac tumor involving th.normalized_text: Extragonadal yolk sac tumor involving the small intestine
Extragonadal yolk sac tumor involving th.description: A malignant germ-cell tumor that can arise at extragonadal sites and typically expresses AFP, glypican-3, and SALL4; it may occasionally mimic an adenocarcinoma.

Bleeding Meckel diverticulum with ectopi.normalized_text: Bleeding Meckel diverticulum with ectopic gastric mucosa
Bleeding Meckel diverticulum with ectopi.description: A congenital ileal diverticulum that may contain acid-secreting gastric mucosa, causing ulceration of adjacent ileal mucosa and painless gastrointestinal bleeding. Technetium-99m pertechnetate imaging can show uptake in ectopic gastric mucosa.

Enteric duplication cyst containing ecto.normalized_text: Enteric duplication cyst containing ectopic gastric mucosa
Enteric duplication cyst containing ecto.description: A congenital duplication of the gastrointestinal tract that can contain ectopic gastric mucosa. Acid secretion can cause mucosal ulceration, bleeding, anemia, and uptake on a technetium-99m pertechnetate scan similar to a Meckel diverticulum.

Peptic ulcer disease with chronic gastro.normalized_text: Peptic ulcer disease with chronic gastrointestinal bleeding
Peptic ulcer disease with chronic gastro.description: Gastric or duodenal ulceration, commonly related to Helicobacter pylori infection or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug exposure, can cause occult or overt blood loss and severe iron-deficiency anemia.

Small-bowel gastrointestinal bleeding fr.normalized_text: Small-bowel gastrointestinal bleeding from a vascular lesion, such as angiodysplasia
Small-bowel gastrointestinal bleeding fr.description: Angiodysplasia is an acquired vascular malformation of the gastrointestinal tract that can produce recurrent occult bleeding and iron-deficiency anemia, particularly when bleeding is intermittent.

diagnoses.name: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia
diagnoses.normalized_text: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia
diagnoses.icd11_title: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia

Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation (PA.description: An abnormal direct connection between a pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein, producing a vascular lung nodule with identifiable feeding and draining vessels. It may be solitary or multiple and is often associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (H.normalized_text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT, Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome) with pulmonary arteriovenous malformations
Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (H.description: An inherited vascular disorder characterized by telangiectasias and visceral arteriovenous malformations, especially in the lungs, liver, brain, and gastrointestinal tract. Pulmonary AVMs may be multiple.

Pulmonary varix (pulmonary venous aneury.description: A focal dilatation of a pulmonary vein that can appear as a round or lobulated pulmonary mass and may mimic a pulmonary AVM. Unlike a PAVM, it usually lacks a distinct feeding artery-to-draining-vein shunt.

Pulmonary artery aneurysm or pseudoaneur.description: A focal dilatation of a pulmonary arterial branch, potentially due to infection, trauma, vasculitis, pulmonary hypertension, or congenital vascular disease. It can present as an enhancing vascular pulmonary nodule.

Pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis.description: A smoking-associated interstitial lung disease characterized by bronchiolocentric Langerhans-cell granulomas that evolve into irregular nodules, cavitary nodules, and upper-lung-predominant cysts.

Pulmonary lymphangioleiomyomatosis.description: A cystic lung disease, usually affecting women, caused by proliferation of abnormal smooth-muscle-like LAM cells and resulting in diffuse thin-walled pulmonary cysts.

Cystic bronchiectasis due to chronic pul.normalized_text: Cystic bronchiectasis due to chronic pulmonary infection
Cystic bronchiectasis due to chronic pul.description: Permanent abnormal dilation of bronchi caused by recurrent or severe airway infection and inflammation; it may produce clustered cystic spaces, chronic cough, and recurrent sputum production.

Post-primary pulmonary tuberculosis.description: Mycobacterial lung infection that commonly involves the upper lobes and can cause cavitation, nodules, fibrosis, systemic symptoms, and bronchogenic spread.

Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopat.normalized_text: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) due to JC virus
Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopat.description: A demyelinating central nervous system infection caused by reactivation of JC polyomavirus, typically occurring in people with impaired cellular immunity such as advanced HIV infection or patients receiving natalizumab.

HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (.description: A spectrum of cognitive, behavioral, and motor impairment related to HIV infection and chronic central nervous system inflammation, ranging from mild neurocognitive disorder to HIV-associated dementia.

Primary central nervous system lymphoma.normalized_text: Primary central nervous system lymphoma associated with HIV
Primary central nervous system lymphoma.description: An Epstein-Barr virus-associated B-cell lymphoma occurring in the brain of severely immunocompromised patients, particularly those with advanced HIV infection.

Cerebral toxoplasmosis.description: A reactivation infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii that produces focal brain lesions in people with severe cellular immunodeficiency, especially advanced HIV infection.

Danon disease (LAMP2-associated lysosoma.description: An X-linked lysosomal/autophagy disorder caused by LAMP2 deficiency. It commonly causes severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, ventricular pre-excitation, conduction abnormalities, skeletal myopathy, and sometimes intellectual disability.

PRKAG2 syndrome.description: An inherited glycogen-storage cardiomyopathy caused by variants in PRKAG2, characterized by ventricular pre-excitation, conduction-system disease, atrial arrhythmias, and hypertrophic-appearing ventricular walls due to myocardial glycogen accumulation.

Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease.normalized_text: Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease type II)
Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease.description: A lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency that causes lysosomal glycogen accumulation, skeletal and respiratory muscle weakness, and cardiomyopathy, especially in infantile-onset disease.

Hydronephrosis.description: Dilation of the renal pelvis and calyces due to impaired urine drainage, commonly caused by ureteral obstruction such as a stone, stricture, or mass.

Obstructive uropathy from ureteral calcu.description: Urinary tract obstruction caused by a ureteral stone, which can produce upstream dilation of the renal collecting system (hydronephrosis).

Parapelvic renal cyst.description: A cyst located in or near the renal sinus that can appear as an anechoic central renal lesion and may mimic hydronephrosis on ultrasound.

Acne conglobata.description: A severe chronic nodulocystic form of acne characterized by extensive inflammatory nodules, abscesses, cysts, comedones, draining sinus tracts, and potential scarring.

Acne fulminans.description: An uncommon, abrupt and highly inflammatory form of severe acne with painful ulcerative nodules and pustules, often accompanied by fever, joint pain, and other systemic symptoms.

Nodulocystic acne.description: A severe acne subtype in which deep inflamed nodules and cysts develop from obstructed and inflamed pilosebaceous follicles, most often affecting the face and upper trunk.

Bacterial folliculitis with furunculosis.description: A bacterial infection of hair follicles, commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus, producing pustules, painful follicular papules, boils, abscesses, and crusting.

Renal cell carcinoma.description: A malignant tumor arising from renal tubular cells, often presenting as a solid enhancing renal mass with heterogeneous areas from necrosis or hemorrhage.

Renal oncocytoma.description: A benign epithelial kidney tumor that can appear as a well-circumscribed solid renal mass and may be difficult to distinguish from renal cell carcinoma on imaging alone.

Angiomyolipoma of the kidney.description: A usually benign renal tumor composed of blood vessels, smooth muscle, and fat. Some lesions contain little visible fat and can mimic renal cell carcinoma.

Renal abscess.description: A localized collection of infection within or around the kidney, usually occurring with urinary infection, fever, flank pain, and inflammatory laboratory abnormalities.

Adrenal mass, including pheochromocytoma.normalized_text: Adrenal mass, including pheochromocytoma or adrenocortical neoplasm
Adrenal mass, including pheochromocytoma.description: Tumors of the adrenal gland can form large heterogeneous masses near the upper pole of the kidney. Pheochromocytoma may produce catecholamines, while adrenocortical tumors may be functioning or nonfunctioning.

Capnocytophaga canimorsus septicemia wit.normalized_text: Capnocytophaga canimorsus septicemia with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and purpura fulminans
Capnocytophaga canimorsus septicemia wit.description: A fulminant bloodstream infection caused by a dog- and cat-associated Gram-negative bacillus. It can cause septic shock, DIC, purpuric skin lesions, multiorgan failure, and severe thrombocytopenia, particularly in patients with impaired splenic function, alcohol use disorder, or immunocompromise.

Purpura fulminans due to severe bacteria.normalized_text: Purpura fulminans due to severe bacterial sepsis
Purpura fulminans due to severe bacteria.description: Purpura fulminans is a rapidly progressive thrombotic skin and coagulation disorder, usually caused by severe sepsis with DIC. It produces widespread purpura, skin necrosis, thrombocytopenia, and multiorgan dysfunction.

Septic shock with disseminated intravasc.normalized_text: Septic shock with disseminated intravascular coagulation
Septic shock with disseminated intravasc.description: Septic shock is life-threatening infection-associated circulatory and metabolic failure. Severe cases can trigger DIC, causing thrombocytopenia, abnormal coagulation tests, microvascular thrombosis, bleeding, hemolysis, and multiorgan injury.

Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP.description: TTP is a thrombotic microangiopathy, usually caused by severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, characterized by thrombocytopenia and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with variable kidney, neurologic, and fever manifestations. Coagulation studies are generally normal.

diagnoses.name: MELAS syndrome
diagnoses.icd11_title: MELAS - [Mitochondrial encephalopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes] syndrome

Acute right middle cerebral artery ische.normalized_text: Acute right middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke
Acute right middle cerebral artery ische.description: An acute infarction caused by interruption of blood flow to the right cerebral hemisphere, commonly from occlusion of the internal carotid artery or middle cerebral artery.

Cardioembolic ischemic stroke due to lef.normalized_text: Cardioembolic ischemic stroke due to left ventricular thrombus
Cardioembolic ischemic stroke due to lef.description: A cerebral infarction caused by embolization of a thrombus formed within the left ventricle, often in the setting of reduced ventricular wall motion, prior myocardial infarction, cardiomyopathy, or ventricular aneurysm.

Left atrial myxoma with cerebral embolic.normalized_text: Left atrial myxoma with cerebral embolic stroke
Left atrial myxoma with cerebral embolic.description: A left atrial myxoma is a benign cardiac tumor that can shed tumor fragments or surface thrombus, causing embolic ischemic stroke and occlusion of cerebral arteries.

Right internal carotid artery occlusion.normalized_text: Right internal carotid artery occlusion with artery-to-artery embolic stroke
Right internal carotid artery occlusion.description: Occlusion of the internal carotid artery, often from atherosclerotic thrombosis, embolism, or less commonly dissection, can produce a large ipsilateral middle cerebral artery territory infarct.

Colangiocarcinoma extrahepático distal.description: Un adenocarcinoma maligno que surge en el conducto biliar extrahepático, que a menudo causa obstrucción biliar progresiva y ictericia.

Adenocarcinoma pancreático ductal de la.normalized_text: Adenocarcinoma pancreático ductal de la cabeza pancreática
Adenocarcinoma pancreático ductal de la.description: Un cáncer de páncreas que surge en la cabeza del páncreas y puede obstruir el conducto biliar común distal, produciendo ictericia obstructiva indolora y un aumento de CA 19-9.

Carcinoma de vesícula biliar con extensi.normalized_text: Carcinoma de vesícula biliar con extensión biliar
Carcinoma de vesícula biliar con extensi.description: Una malignidad de la vesícula biliar, generalmente adenocarcinoma, que puede invadir el hígado o los conductos biliares extrahepáticos y causar ictericia obstructiva.

Obstrucción biliar extrahepática benigna.normalized_text: Obstrucción biliar extrahepática benigna, como la coledocolitiasi o la estenosis biliar inflamatoria
Obstrucción biliar extrahepática benigna.description: La obstrucción del conducto biliar común por una piedra, lodo o estenosis benigna puede causar ictericia y elevación de enzimas hepáticas colestáticas; CA 19-9 puede aumentar modestamente durante la obstrucción.

Acute appendicitis.description: Inflammation of the appendix, usually caused by obstruction of the appendiceal lumen. MRI may show a dilated, thick-walled appendix with surrounding inflammatory change.

Crohn disease involving the terminal ile.normalized_text: Crohn disease involving the terminal ileum
Crohn disease involving the terminal ile.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that commonly affects the terminal ileum and may produce segmental bowel-wall thickening, mucosal hyperenhancement, edema, strictures, and surrounding mesenteric inflammation.

Terminal ileitis due to infectious enter.normalized_text: Terminal ileitis due to infectious enteritis
Terminal ileitis due to infectious enter.description: Acute inflammation of the terminal ileum caused by gastrointestinal infection, including organisms such as Yersinia, Campylobacter, or Salmonella. It can mimic appendicitis on imaging.

Lateral tibial plateau fracture.description: A fracture involving the upper surface of the tibia at the knee joint, often caused by axial loading or valgus force and sometimes associated with depression of the lateral joint surface.

Post-traumatic lateral tibial plateau de.description: Residual contour deformity or articular surface depression after a prior tibial plateau fracture, which may predispose to later knee pain and osteoarthritis.

Early post-traumatic osteoarthritis of t.normalized_text: Early post-traumatic osteoarthritis of the knee
Early post-traumatic osteoarthritis of t.description: Degenerative wear of knee cartilage and subchondral bone that can develop after previous joint injury, especially after an intra-articular tibial plateau fracture.

Trichostasis spinulosa.description: A follicular disorder in which multiple retained vellus hairs and keratin accumulate within dilated hair follicles, producing dark, rough, comedo-like follicular papules.

Keratosis pilaris.description: A common benign keratinization disorder characterized by keratin plugging of hair follicles, typically causing rough follicular papules on the upper arms, thighs, buttocks, or cheeks.

Comedonal acne.description: Acne characterized predominantly by open comedones (blackheads) and closed comedones caused by follicular obstruction with keratin and sebum.

Folliculitis.description: Inflammation of hair follicles, often caused by bacterial, fungal, mechanical, or occlusive factors, which usually presents with follicular red papules or pustules.

Pili multigemini.description: A hair-follicle developmental abnormality in which several hair shafts arise from a single follicular opening, producing grouped hairs and sometimes follicular papules.

Livedoid vasculopathy.description: A thrombotic disorder of small dermal blood vessels causing recurrent painful ulcers around the ankles and lower legs, often healing with white stellate scars called atrophie blanche.

Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa.description: A necrotizing vasculitis affecting small- and medium-sized arteries in the skin, commonly producing tender nodules, livedo reticularis, purpura, and painful leg ulcers.

Pyoderma gangrenosum.description: An inflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis that causes rapidly progressive painful ulcers, typically with a purulent base and undermined violaceous borders; it may be associated with inflammatory bowel disease, arthritis, or blood disorders.

Venous stasis ulcer.description: A chronic lower-leg ulcer caused by venous insufficiency and venous hypertension, usually occurring around the medial ankle with edema, brown hemosiderin staining, and stasis dermatitis.

diagnoses.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
diagnoses.icd11_title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour of unspecified gastrointestinal sites

Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.description: A rare malignant vascular tumor composed of epithelioid endothelial cells, often arranged in cords or nests within a myxohyaline stroma. Intracytoplasmic vacuoles or primitive vascular lumina are characteristic, and endothelial markers such as CD31, CD34, ERG, or FLI1 are typically positive.

Epithelioid angiosarcoma.description: An aggressive malignant endothelial tumor with markedly atypical epithelioid cells and variable vasoformative spaces. It commonly expresses vascular markers including CD31, ERG, FLI1, and sometimes CD34.

Epithelioid hemangioma.description: A benign or locally aggressive vascular neoplasm composed of plump epithelioid endothelial cells lining well-formed vessels, often accompanied by inflammation, especially eosinophils.

Metastatic carcinoma with epithelioid mo.description: A metastatic epithelial malignancy can form nests or cords of atypical epithelioid cells and may mimic a vascular tumor, particularly when the primary site is unknown. Carcinomas usually express broad-spectrum cytokeratins and epithelial membrane antigen rather than endothelial markers.

diagnoses.name: Malignant gastrointestinal stromal tumor
diagnoses.icd11_title: Malignant GIST - [gastrointestinal stromal tumour] of large intestine

Pancreatoblastoma.description: A rare malignant pancreatic tumor with acinar differentiation, classically seen in children but also occurring rarely in adults. It often presents as a large, well-circumscribed heterogeneous pancreatic mass with necrosis or hemorrhage. Histology may show acinar-like cells and characteristic squamoid corpuscles.

Acinar cell carcinoma of the pancreas.normalized_text: Acinar cell carcinoma of the pancreas
Acinar cell carcinoma of the pancreas.description: An uncommon malignant exocrine pancreatic neoplasm composed of cells showing acinar enzyme-producing differentiation. Tumors are often large, sharply demarcated, and may contain hemorrhage and necrosis.

Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of the pa.normalized_text: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of the pancreas
Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of the pa.description: A low-grade malignant pancreatic neoplasm that usually affects young women and is often large, encapsulated, and composed of solid and hemorrhagic-cystic areas. Microscopically it commonly forms pseudopapillary structures around delicate blood vessels.

Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.description: A neoplasm arising from pancreatic neuroendocrine cells. Large nonfunctioning tumors can present as well-circumscribed pancreatic masses with necrosis, hemorrhage, and mass effect on adjacent organs.

Segmental (localized) Darier disease.description: A localized mosaic form of Darier disease, a keratinization disorder characterized by keratotic crusted papules and plaques with histologic acantholytic dyskeratosis.

Acantholytic dyskeratotic epidermal nevu.description: A rare epidermal nevus presenting as a localized, often unilateral verrucous keratotic plaque, with biopsy findings resembling Darier disease or Hailey-Hailey disease.

Hailey-Hailey disease.description: An inherited acantholytic blistering disorder that commonly affects intertriginous areas such as the axillae, causing recurrent painful erosions, fissures, and crusting.

Grover disease (transient acantholytic d.description: An acquired eruption of itchy keratotic papules, usually on the trunk, with focal acantholysis and sometimes dyskeratosis on biopsy.

Hypertrophic lichen planus.description: A chronic inflammatory skin disease that may produce thick, intensely hyperkeratotic, hyperpigmented plaques, often with excoriation and crusting.

Conventional chondrosarcoma of the ilium.description: A malignant cartilage-producing bone tumor, commonly arising in the pelvis in adults. Imaging often shows a large lobulated expansile bone lesion with chondroid matrix calcifications, cortical destruction, and an associated soft-tissue component.

Low-grade chondrosarcoma (atypical carti.description: A relatively low-grade malignant cartilage tumor that can be difficult to distinguish from enchondroma. In the pelvis, even histologically low-grade cartilaginous tumors are generally considered malignant because of their locally aggressive behavior.

Enchondroma.description: A benign intramedullary cartilage tumor that usually occurs in the small bones of the hands and feet but can rarely arise in the pelvis. It may contain chondroid calcifications but generally lacks aggressive destruction.

Chondromyxoid fibroma.description: A rare benign but locally aggressive bone tumor composed of chondroid, myxoid, and fibrous tissue. It usually affects younger patients and often appears as an eccentric expansile lytic lesion, occasionally with cortical thinning.

Classical stiff-person syndrome (anti-GA.description: A rare autoimmune neurologic disorder characterized by progressive axial and limb rigidity, painful muscle spasms, and exaggerated startle responses, frequently associated with high-titer glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD65) antibodies.

Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigid.normalized_text: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM)
Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigid.description: A severe stiff-person-spectrum autoimmune disorder causing rigidity, stimulus-sensitive spasms, myoclonus, brainstem dysfunction, autonomic instability, and sometimes encephalopathy; it is often associated with glycine-receptor antibodies but may also occur with GAD antibodies.

Isaacs syndrome (acquired neuromyotonia).description: A peripheral nerve hyperexcitability disorder, often autoimmune, producing muscle stiffness, twitching, cramps, myokymia, delayed muscle relaxation, and continuous motor activity on EMG. It may be associated with CASPR2 or LGI1 antibodies.

Hereditary spastic paraplegia.description: A group of inherited neurodegenerative disorders characterized by slowly progressive lower-limb spasticity, weakness, gait impairment, and hyperreflexia due to corticospinal tract dysfunction.

Giant cell arteritis.description: A granulomatous vasculitis of medium and large arteries, usually affecting adults older than 50 years. Involvement of temporal and other external carotid branches can cause scalp ischemia, ulceration, and necrosis.

Takayasu arteritis.description: A chronic large-vessel vasculitis involving the aorta and its major branches, commonly causing stenosis or occlusion of the subclavian and carotid arteries. Severe cranial arterial hypoperfusion can rarely cause scalp necrosis.

Atherosclerotic carotid or subclavian ar.normalized_text: Atherosclerotic carotid or subclavian artery occlusive disease
Atherosclerotic carotid or subclavian ar.description: Progressive plaque-related narrowing of major arteries can reduce cerebral and scalp perfusion, especially when carotid, subclavian, or external carotid circulation is severely compromised.

Scalp infarction from external carotid a.normalized_text: Scalp infarction from external carotid artery ischemia
Scalp infarction from external carotid a.description: A localized ischemic injury of the scalp caused by severe compromise of the external carotid circulation, which may result from vasculitis, thrombosis, embolism, arterial dissection, or critical proximal arterial stenosis.

Cold agglutinin disease (cold autoimmune.normalized_text: Cold agglutinin disease (cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia)
Cold agglutinin disease (cold autoimmune.description: An autoimmune hemolytic anemia caused by IgM antibodies that bind red blood cells at cooler temperatures, producing red-cell agglutination and complement-mediated hemolysis.

Autoimmune hemolytic anemia (warm antibo.description: Hemolytic anemia caused by autoantibodies, usually IgG, binding red blood cells at body temperature and leading to splenic destruction of red cells.

Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction due.normalized_text: Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction due to ABO incompatibility
Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction due.description: A severe immune-mediated reaction occurring when incompatible donor red blood cells are transfused, causing rapid intravascular hemolysis, hemoglobinemia, and sometimes red-cell agglutination.

Paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria.description: A rare complement-mediated autoimmune hemolytic anemia caused by biphasic Donath-Landsteiner antibodies, often triggered by cold exposure or infection and characterized by episodic intravascular hemolysis.

Necrobiosis lipoidica.description: A chronic granulomatous skin disorder, often associated with diabetes mellitus, characterized by yellow-brown or orange atrophic plaques with erythematous violaceous borders, usually on the shins. Histology commonly shows layered palisading granulomatous inflammation surrounding degenerated collagen (necrobiosis).

Granuloma annulare.description: A benign inflammatory dermatosis producing annular papules or plaques, often on the hands, feet, elbows, or other extremities. Histology can show palisading granulomas around foci of altered collagen and mucin.

Cutaneous sarcoidosis.description: Skin involvement by sarcoidosis, a systemic granulomatous disease. Cutaneous lesions may present as red-brown, violaceous, papular, nodular, or plaque-like lesions and typically show noncaseating granulomas on biopsy.

Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma.description: A rare chronic xanthogranulomatous disorder, frequently associated with paraproteinemia or hematologic disease. It commonly produces yellow-red indurated plaques or nodules, often around the eyes, with necrobiosis and xanthomatous inflammation on histology.

Rheumatoid nodule / palisaded neutrophil.normalized_text: Rheumatoid nodule / palisaded neutrophilic granulomatous dermatitis
Rheumatoid nodule / palisaded neutrophil.description: Rheumatoid nodules and related palisaded granulomatous dermatoses may occur in patients with rheumatoid arthritis or other systemic inflammatory diseases. They can show palisading histiocytes surrounding necrobiotic collagen or fibrin.

Pseudohipoparatiroidismo tipo 1B (PHP1B).description: Un trastorno de la resistencia a la hormona paratiroidea, especialmente en el túbulo proximal renal, comúnmente causado por una metilación anormal en el locus GNAS. Produce hipocalcemia, hiperfosfatemia y PTH elevada a pesar de una secreción de PTH normal o aumentada.

Pseudohipoparatiroidismo tipo 1A (PHP1A,.normalized_text: Pseudohipoparatiroidismo tipo 1A (PHP1A, osteodistrofia hereditaria de Albright con resistencia hormonal)
Pseudohipoparatiroidismo tipo 1A (PHP1A,.description: Un trastorno de la región codificante GNAS que causa resistencia a la PTH y, a menudo, a otras hormonas como la TSH. Normalmente causa hipocalcemia, hiperfosfatemia y PTH elevada, a menudo con características físicas de osteodistrofia hereditaria de Albright.

Enfermedad renal crónica con hiperparati.normalized_text: Enfermedad renal crónica con hiperparatiroidismo secundario
Enfermedad renal crónica con hiperparati.description: La reducción de la excreción de fosfato renal y la disminución de la producción de calcitriol en la enfermedad renal crónica pueden causar hiperfosfatemia, hipocalcemia y elevación secundaria de la PTH.

Deficiencia de vitamina D o alteración d.normalized_text: Deficiencia de vitamina D o alteración de la activación de la vitamina D
Deficiencia de vitamina D o alteración d.description: La insuficiente vitamina D disminuye la absorción intestinal de calcio y causa hiperparatiroidismo secundario. El fosfato suele ser bajo o normal porque una PTH elevada favorece la excreción urinaria de fosfato.

Hipoparatiroidismo primario.description: La secreción deficiente de PTH, debida a causas autoinmunes, postquirúrgicas, genéticas o infiltrativas, produce hipocalcemia e hiperfosfatemia.

Disseminated histoplasmosis.description: Systemic infection with Histoplasma capsulatum, often involving the reticuloendothelial system, liver, spleen, bone marrow, and lungs. Severe disease can cause pancytopenia, hepatitis, renal dysfunction, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.

Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocyt.normalized_text: Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), potentially triggered by disseminated fungal infection
Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocyt.description: A life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by excessive immune activation, commonly triggered by infection, malignancy, or autoimmune disease. It can produce cytopenias, liver injury, coagulopathy, high LDH, hypofibrinogenemia, and multiorgan dysfunction.

Disseminated intravascular coagulation (.normalized_text: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) due to severe systemic infection or inflammation
Disseminated intravascular coagulation (.description: An acquired consumptive coagulopathy in which widespread activation of coagulation causes depletion of platelets and clotting factors, thrombosis, bleeding risk, and organ injury. It is often caused by severe infection, malignancy, trauma, or systemic inflammatory illness.

Visceral leishmaniasis.description: A systemic protozoal infection that infiltrates macrophages in the spleen, liver, and bone marrow. It classically causes fever, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, hypergammaglobulinemia, liver dysfunction, and can occasionally trigger HLH or coagulopathy.

Ovarian steroid cell tumor, not otherwis.normalized_text: Ovarian steroid cell tumor, not otherwise specified
Ovarian steroid cell tumor, not otherwis.description: A rare sex cord-stromal ovarian tumor composed of steroid-producing cells, often with clear or vacuolated cytoplasm. It may produce androgens or other steroid hormones and can occasionally behave malignantly.

Ovarian Leydig cell tumor.description: A rare benign or low-grade ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor derived from Leydig cells, commonly androgen-secreting and usually presenting as a small unilateral ovarian mass.

Ovarian clear cell carcinoma.description: An epithelial ovarian carcinoma characterized by clear cytoplasm, hobnail cells, and variable glandular or solid growth. It may present as an adnexal mass and is often associated with endometriosis.

Metastatic renal cell carcinoma to the o.normalized_text: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma to the ovary
Metastatic renal cell carcinoma to the o.description: Renal cell carcinoma, particularly clear cell type, can rarely metastasize to the ovary and may resemble a primary ovarian clear-cell neoplasm because of its clear, vascular tumor cells.

Familial isolated syringomyelia.description: A rare inherited form of syringomyelia in which a fluid-filled cavity (syrinx) develops within the spinal cord without an obvious secondary cause such as trauma, tumor, or Chiari malformation. The pedigree is compatible with autosomal-recessive inheritance.

Syringomyelia associated with Chiari I m.normalized_text: Syringomyelia associated with Chiari I malformation
Syringomyelia associated with Chiari I m.description: Syringomyelia may occur when downward displacement of the cerebellar tonsils at the foramen magnum disrupts cerebrospinal-fluid flow, producing a syrinx in the cervical spinal cord.

Hydromyelia.description: Hydromyelia is dilation of the central canal of the spinal cord by cerebrospinal fluid. It can resemble syringomyelia on MRI and may be difficult to distinguish when the cavity is small and centrally located.

Intramedullary spinal cord tumor with se.normalized_text: Intramedullary spinal cord tumor with secondary syrinx, such as ependymoma
Intramedullary spinal cord tumor with se.description: An intramedullary tumor, particularly an ependymoma, can obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow or alter cord architecture and produce an associated syrinx above or below the tumor.

Posterior reversible encephalopathy synd.description: A clinicoradiologic syndrome of vasogenic brain edema, often related to severe hypertension, renal failure, eclampsia, immunosuppressive therapy, or endothelial injury. It commonly affects the parieto-occipital regions and may include small hemorrhages or areas of restricted diffusion.

Cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related infl.description: An inflammatory reaction around amyloid-laden cortical and leptomeningeal vessels in older adults. MRI typically shows asymmetric or multifocal white-matter edema, lobar cerebral microbleeds, and sometimes small ischemic lesions.

Cerebral fat embolism syndrome.description: A complication of long-bone or pelvic fractures, orthopedic surgery, or major trauma in which fat emboli cause multifocal cerebral ischemia and microhemorrhage. Diffusion MRI may show multiple scattered punctate restricted-diffusion lesions, sometimes called a starfield pattern.

Embolic ischemic strokes with hemorrhagi.normalized_text: Embolic ischemic strokes with hemorrhagic transformation
Embolic ischemic strokes with hemorrhagi.description: Multiple emboli from a cardiac, aortic, or other vascular source can produce scattered bilateral acute ischemic infarcts. Small infarcts may develop petechial hemorrhage, particularly with reperfusion or anticoagulation.

Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with ve.normalized_text: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with venous infarction
Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with ve.description: Thrombosis of cerebral venous sinuses or cortical veins causes impaired venous drainage, resulting in cortical-subcortical edema, infarction that may not respect arterial territories, and frequent hemorrhagic components.

Spinal neurosarcoidosis.description: Sarcoidosis involving the spinal cord, characterized by noncaseating granulomatous inflammation that can cause intramedullary cervical cord lesions and enhancement on MRI.

Tuberculous myelitis or intramedullary s.normalized_text: Tuberculous myelitis or intramedullary spinal tuberculoma
Tuberculous myelitis or intramedullary s.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving the spinal cord, which may produce granulomas, cord swelling, and enhancing intramedullary lesions.

Fungal granulomatous myelitis.description: A fungal infection of the central nervous system, such as histoplasmosis or cryptococcosis, that can rarely cause granulomatous spinal cord inflammation and enhancing lesions.

Pulmonary actinomycosis.description: A chronic bacterial infection caused by Actinomyces species, often producing mass-like consolidation, abscesses, cavitation, and suppurative granulomatous inflammation with sulfur-granule-like colonies on pathology.

Pulmonary nocardiosis.description: An opportunistic infection caused by Nocardia bacteria that may cause nodules, consolidation, cavitation, lung abscesses, and suppurative inflammation, particularly in immunocompromised patients.

Pulmonary tuberculosis.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the lung, which can produce cavitary lesions and granulomatous inflammation; upper-lung involvement is most typical, although lower-lobe disease can occur.

Necrotizing bacterial pneumonia or lung.normalized_text: Necrotizing bacterial pneumonia or lung abscess
Necrotizing bacterial pneumonia or lung.description: A severe bacterial pulmonary infection causing localized pus formation, tissue necrosis, cavitation, and surrounding consolidation; common pathogens include anaerobes, Staphylococcus aureus, and Klebsiella species.

Cavitating primary lung carcinoma, espec.normalized_text: Cavitating primary lung carcinoma, especially squamous cell carcinoma
Cavitating primary lung carcinoma, espec.description: A primary lung cancer that may appear as a cavitary mass or consolidative lesion. Tumor necrosis can cause cavitation, and inflammatory tissue around the lesion may obscure the malignancy.

Ascariasis (Ascaris lumbricoides infecti.description: Intestinal infection caused by the large roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides. The image is consistent with a cross-section of an adult nematode, showing a thick cuticle, muscular body wall, intestinal tract, and reproductive structures.
